title: Chananya son of Chizkiya son of Garon (or Gurion)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hananiah son of Hezekiah son of Garon or Gurion. Hyman describes him as the leading figure of the generation of Hillel and Shammai and credits him with preserving Ezekiel and Megillat Taanit. In [Shabbat 13b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.13b.8), Rav Yehudah says in Rav’s name: “Remember that man for good. His name was Hananiah son of Hezekiah. Without him the book of Ezekiel would have been put away.” They brought him three hundred jars of oil and he sat in an upper chamber and expounded the book. [Chagigah 13a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.13a.12) gives the same account.

[Menachot 45a](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.45a.19) reads Hanina son of Hezekiah. [Shabbat 13b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.13b.4) says Hananiah son of Hezekiah and his company wrote Megillat Taanit, for they cherished times of trouble. Hyman cites the end of the scroll for its attribution to Eleazar son of Hananiah son of Hezekiah son of Garon. He is certain both are true and father and son wrote it. [Mishnah Shabbat 1:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Mishnah_Shabbat.1.4) records that those who went up to visit Hananiah son of Hezekiah son of Gurion counted the votes and Beit Shammai outnumbered Beit Hillel. They issued eighteen decrees that day.

The corresponding [Shabbat 13b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.13b.2) reads Garon. [Chagigah 13a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.13a.13) describes a child who understood the hashmal, from which fire came out and burned him. Hananiah son of Hezekiah replied, “If this child was wise, is everyone wise?”
Hyman discusses his son Eleazar in a separate entry.[^1]

notes.text: [Hyman, vol. II, p. 506](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/60/Aaron_Hyman._Toldoth_Tannaim_veAmoraim._II._1910.pdf#page=89) gives Shabbat 13a for the Garon form that is found in the consulted 13b. Mishnah Shabbat has Giryon. The final attribution of the scroll and the adjacent abbreviation שר׳ in Hyman’s notice remain unresolved. [Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1512&lang=en) also discusses the different attributions, and gives wine where the consulted Talmud passages give oil.
